correctness.rationale: For E=Lambda(F_q^4), q odd, even components central and each input has 8 even coordinates, giving q^16 free pairs. Writing odd input u+alpha, v+beta, the commutator is exactly 2(u wedge v+u wedge beta+alpha wedge v). The six degree-two coordinates satisfy the one Plucker Pfaffian equation iff decomposable. A fixed nonzero bivector has q(q²−1) ordered u,v pairs, while the zero bivector has q^4+(q^4−1)q dependent pairs. The top-degree linear form on 8 alpha/beta variables is rank one for (u,v)!=(0,0), yielding q^7 inputs per t, and rank zero for the zero pair, yielding the exceptional zero-fiber q^8. These facts yield all four cases and commuting probability q^(-4)+q^(-5)-q^(-9). Alternating rank<=4 gives width two, and rank four forbids width one. An independently coded F3 wedge-frequency enumeration found exactly 261 output bivectors, zero pair count 321 and each nonzero simple fiber 24, matching q formulas. This finite test corroborates, not replaces, the proof for all odd prime powers.
